$comment: Machine-readable roll-up of every load-bearing claim FINALTab makes, each tied to how it was
measured. If a claim is not in this file, it is not backed. If a claim is in this file with
state UNPROVEN or BLOCKED, the project says so publicly rather than implying otherwise.
Claims measured on 2026-08-10 below are historical V1 evidence unless explicitly scoped otherwise.
Current V2 deployment and value-moving proof are recorded in currentRelease and their separate manifests.
scope: Current V2 release plus explicitly archived V1 evidence
historicalEvidenceCommitNote: Measured against commit d4dfb7e PLUS an uncommitted working tree (7 modified tracked files, 3 untracked at the time of the run: the MCP agent-settlement path and this docs pass). Not a clean-checkout result: re-running these commands on a fresh clone of d4dfb7e produces the pre-MCP numbers, not these.

mcp.walletModel: external debtor wallets plus a wallet-signed short-lived broadcast approval

durableSubmissionJournal.acceptedReplay: returns the durable execution without simulation or execution
durableSubmissionJournal.preparedRecovery: reuses the stored successful simulation and deterministic idempotency key under a bounded persisted approval expiry

mcp.deployedBaselineProbe: The superseded b084497 deployment passed unauthenticated rejection, MCP 2.0.0, arbitrary-participant planning, cent-perfect calculation, and proof binding. It does not prove the current nine-tool deployment.

usdcSettlement.caveat: Explicitly authorized disposable Base Sepolia signer material was used by a simulate-then-single-broadcast runner. This proves the V2 contract/KeeperHub rail, not the production MCP human broadcast-challenge path.

supabase.caveat: The baseline plus five ordered additive migrations, 29-table RLS schema, sensitive RPC privilege matrix, advisor result, durable quotas, spend reservations, and sensitive provider configuration are proven. The post-promotion cutover is not applied. Cross-device application, shared-journal behavior, provider behavior, and other live flows remain unclaimed until the candidate is deployed and probed.

agentControl.memory: bounded expiring user-deletable audit memory; cannot modify code, policy, prompts, or authorization

labels.LIVE_PROVEN: A real external system was contacted and the response is recorded.
labels.LOCAL_PROVEN: The current local candidate passed reproducible checks but has not been deployed and live-probed.
labels.FIXTURE_PROVEN: Exercised only against local fixtures or mocked module boundaries.
labels.LIVE_EXERCISED_FAILED: A real external call was made and returned a real failure. The surface is proven; the success is not.
labels.BLOCKED: Cannot be proven without an action outside autonomous scope.
labels.UNPROVEN: Code exists, no evidence either way.
labels.NOT_APPLIED: Written but never installed or run anywhere.

claims.method: Demo-signer balances read from Base Sepolia before and after each settlement; receipt fetched independently from https://sepolia.base.org rather than trusted from KeeperHub; conservation asserted. Full records in proof-output/live-proof-*.json.
claims.correction: Earlier revisions marked this claim BLOCKED pending a contracts/scripts/fund-relayer.js deployer sweep into the relayer 0x7ae891ec51990684682a084381e97b59d787652b. What actually happened: the sweep was deliberately never run; instead the relayer was funded 0.00005 ETH directly (tx 0xce5ec0bf..., block 45310097) after KeeperHub reported 'Insufficient BASE balance. Have: 0.0, Need: 0.000000231.' Separately, every recorded executeSettlement execution reports sponsored: true with gas paid from KeeperHub's own gas-payer EOA 0xdcf4bac4bd805948168ff63483bc493894a29613 through its forwarder 0x5af5194b4b0909eb978e3cf1e25333852277f07d - so the measured records show KeeperHub-sponsored gas on the settlements themselves. After the user explicitly authorized testnet funding of the demo signer addresses, four settlements executed executeSettlement on the deployed contract against real Base Sepolia USDC. The defect also recorded in the earlier entry (demo signers reminted per page load) was real, was fixed in apps/web/lib/demoKeys.ts before any funding landed, and that fix plus its in-browser verification stand.
claims.behaviourWhenBlocked: Unchanged and still enforced: if simulation fails, the app renders 'WOULD REVERT - NOT BROADCAST', no cached receipt is replayed, and no success is implied.

claims.claim: Receipt extraction and natural-language allocation work against a live model

claims.claim: The model cascade falls Groq -> Claude -> OpenAI
claims.value: 12 cascade tests driving the real router with each SDK mocked at the module boundary
claims.caveat: Only the Groq leg has ever contacted a real API. No Claude or OpenAI key is configured, so those two legs are tested, not proven. The OpenAI leg previously requested 'gpt-4-vision', which is not a served model id; it now requests 'gpt-4o' via OPENAI_VISION_MODEL. That correction is reasoned, not measured, because the leg still has no key.

claims.claim: Debtors produce valid EIP-3009 receiveWithAuthorization signatures
claims.value: Sign button exercised in a real browser session against the running app; produces valid signatures
claims.caveat: Demo keys only. A prior revision of the docs called this a silent-failure blocker; live testing disproved that.

claims.claim: Demo debtor addresses can be made stable across reloads so a funded testnet address survives
claims.value: With NEXT_PUBLIC_FINALTAB_PERSIST_DEMO_KEYS=1 the three demo addresses are byte-identical across a browser reload; with the flag unset they rotate on every load and nothing is written to localStorage. Both branches exercised in a real browser session against the running dev server.
claims.implementation: apps/web/lib/demoKeys.ts (localStorage key finaltab.demo-signers.v1), surfaced by apps/web/components/FundingPanel.tsx
claims.tests: 46 unit tests in apps/web/test/demoKeys.test.ts, including a source-level regression guard that the flag is read as the literal process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FINALTAB_PERSIST_DEMO_KEYS member expression, because Next.js substitutes public env vars by matching that exact text and a unit test cannot observe bundler output.
claims.caveat: Persistence writes throwaway private keys to localStorage in plaintext. Off by default, opt-in, labelled in the UI, and only ever acceptable for disposable Base Sepolia identities. It does not itself unblock settle.onchain - it only makes the addresses fundable.

claims.claim: No secrets are live in the working tree
claims.value: A deployer private key was committed across six judge-facing docs and an Alchemy API key across four files. Both are redacted in the working tree; hardhat.config.js is now env-driven via BASE_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL with a public fallback.
claims.residualRisk: Local only, and narrower than this file previously stated. Corrected 2026-08-10: an earlier revision said both keys 'remain in git history at commit 1f20560'. That was measured and found false - git show 1f20560:SUBMISSION.md returns no key, and its only 64-hex token is the public Basescan tx hash. Both credentials do survive on this machine, but exclusively in unreachable objects.
claims.historyScan: Walked the entire object database rather than the commit graph: 190 blobs total (git cat-file --batch-all-objects), 305 objects reachable from all refs (git rev-list --objects --all), 38 unreachable (git fsck --unreachable --dangling). The deployer key appears in 8 blobs, every one unreachable. The Alchemy key appears only in unreachable blobs, inside base-sepolia.g.alchemy.com/v2/<key> URLs. Reachable objects containing either key: 0. Service-key shapes (gsk_, alcht_, xai-, nvapi-, sk-proj-, sk-ant-) across all 190 blobs: 0 matches.
claims.exposure: Git transfers only objects reachable from the refs being sent, so no clone, fetch, or push of github.com/vaibhav4046/finaltab can recover either credential. The deployer key is genuine - a local one-way key-to-address derivation (no signing, no broadcast) resolves it to 0x976EF25623A94F6F70924816697C7c7172210a5F, matching the documented deployer - and its blast radius is testnet dust with zero authority over the deployed contract.
claims.remediation: git reflog expire --expire-unreachable=now --all && git gc --prune=now. This touches no commit and changes no hash, so filter-repo is both unnecessary and the wrong tool. Rotating the Alchemy key remains worthwhile and is a user action. Neither was performed here.
claims.caveat: No secret value, prefix, or length is printed anywhere in this repo's documentation.

outOfScope: Rotating credentials or rewriting git history
Funding any mainnet account (the archived V1 signer funding was explicitly user-authorized)
